contents.html_ja: ピアアクセス実施（PAE）プロセスは、PAA プロセスで行われたアクセス制御の決定を継続的に実施するためのものです。PAE は、PDU の属性で表現される、データパケットのセキュリティ上の機微度が、PAA の間に決定された、許容されるセキュリティ属性の集合に収まるかどうかを判定します。実施メカニズムは、ピアのセキュリティプロトコル（SP）がデータを転送しようとするときに関与します。PAE の処理一式がすべて必要になるのは、特定のデータに付されたラベル（インポートされるものもエクスポートされるものも）が明示的なラベルである場合だけです。暗黙的なラベル付けが使われている場合は、PAE の限定された一部分だけが使用され、PAA プロセスが十分なアクセス制御の保証を提供します。
contents.html: The Peer Access Enforcement (PAE) process provides for the continuous enforcement of the access control decision made in the PAA process. PAE determines if the security sensitivity of a data packet, represented in a PDU’s attributes, falls within an allowable set of security attributes determined during PAA. The enforcement mechanism becomes involved when peer Security Protocols (SP) attempt to transfer data. The full suite of PAE processing is only required when the label contained on a specific piece of data (either imported or exported) is an explicit label. When implicit labeling is being used, only a limited subset of PAE is used, the PAA process provides sufficient access control assurance.

contents.html_ja: PAE プロセスは、その機能を実行するために SP から呼び出されます。SP は、受信および送信されるすべてのデータパケットに対する門番として動作します。SP は処理のためにパケットを受信すると、適切なポインタが設定されているかを確認します（パケットの送受信には TEK が使用されます。KID が使用される場合もありますが、これは TEK へのポインタにすぎません）。このポインタが設定されていない場合、SP はエラー状態に入り、パケットを破棄します（実装によっては、任意の回復を試みることができます。その場合、処理中のパケットをキャッシュし、関連付けを確立するために処理を KMP に移すことがあります）。SP の処理の適切な時点で、PAE プロセスが呼び出されて処理を実行します。図 4.3 は、PAE プロセスが実行する機能を示しています。PAE プロセスは結果（PAE_Result = Pass/Fail）を出し、それが SP に返されます。SP が実行しなければならない残りの処理を決定するのは、この結果です。以降の節で PAE プロセスの詳細を説明します。
contents.html: The PAE process is called from the SP to perform its functionality. The SP acts as a gate keeper for all data packets, both incoming and outgoing. When the SP receives a packet for processing it checks to see if the appropriate pointer is in place (a TEK is used when sending and receiving a packet, the KID may be used but this is only a pointer to the TEK). If this pointer is not in place the SP will enter an error condition and drop the packet (some implementations may allow for an optional recovery attempt to be made, the packet being processed may be cached with the processing being transferred to KMP in an attempt to establish an association). At the appropriate time in the SP processing the PAE process will be called to perform its processing. Figure 4.3 illustrates the functions which the PAE process will perform. The PAE process will yield a result (PAE_Result = Pass/Fail) which will be returned to the SP. It is this result which will determine the remainder of the processing which the SP must perform. The following sections describe the details of the PAE process.

contents.html_ja: EV の取得の機能は、使用されている暗号上の関連付けに適した EV を見つけるために、利用可能な EV MIB を検索します。この機能は、PDU 属性に含まれる適切な情報（たとえば、KID、TEK 識別子）を用いて、有効な EV を見つけようとします。有効な EV が見つかれば、EV_Found = Yes となり、EV と PDU 属性が EV と PDU 属性の比較の機能に送られ、その機能が処理を実行します。有効な EV が見つからなければ、EV_Found = No となり、エラー状態が発生します。このエラー状態によりパケットは破棄され、処理は SP に戻されます（実装によっては、任意の回復の試みを許す場合があります。その場合、処理中のパケットをキャッシュし、処理を KMP に移して関連付けの確立を試みることがあります）。
contents.html: The Obtain EV function will search the available EV MIB in an attempt to find the correct EV for the cryptographic association which is being used. This function will use the appropriate information contained in the PDU’s attributes (e.g., KID, TEK identifier) to try and find a valid EV. If a valid EV is found then EV_Found = Yes, and the EV and PDU’s attributes are sent to the Compare EV and PDU Attributes function so that it can perform its processing. If a valid EV is not found then EV_Found = No, and an error condition occurs. This error condition will drop the packet and return processing back to the SP (some implementations may allow for an optional recovery attempt to be made, the packet being processed may be cached with the processing being transferred to KMP in an attempt to establish an association).

contents.html_ja: EV と PDU 属性の比較の機能は、PDU 属性に含まれるデータパケットのセキュリティ属性が、EV で指定された範囲に収まるかどうかを判定します。この機能は、EV との比較に適した PDU 属性の解釈を決定するために、ローカル構成情報を使用します。解釈された PDU 属性は、EV と比較されます。PDU 属性のフィールドが EV に含まれる範囲に収まれば、PAE_Result = Pass となります。PDU 属性のフィールドが EV に含まれる範囲を超えていれば、PAE_Result = Fail となります。その後、PAE からの退出の機能が呼び出されて処理を実行します。
contents.html: The Compare EV and PDU Attributes function will determine whether or not the security attributes of a data packet, contained in the PDU’s attributes, fall within the bounds specified in the EV. This function uses the local configuration information to determine the interpretation of the PDU’s attributes appropriate for comparing with the EV. Once interpreted, the PDU’s attributes are compared to the EV. If the fields in the PDU’s attributes fall within the bounds contained in the EV, then PAE_Result = Pass. If the fields in the PDU’s attributes exceed the bounds contained in the EV, then PAE_Result = Fail. The Exit PAE function is then called to perform its processing.

contents.html_ja: 複数の受信者が指定されている場合、アクセス制御チェック（PAA と PAE の手順の呼び出しを含みます）が受信者ごとに実行されます。マルチキャストメッセージの各受信者へのメッセージ転送は、別個の EV によって支配されます。マルチキャストメッセージの一部の受信者についてアクセス制御チェックが失敗しても、チェックに成功した受信者へのメッセージの送信を妨げる必要はありません。発信者には、（ローカルの実装とポリシーによって）メッセージの 1 人以上の受信者がアクセス制御上の理由で受け入れられないときに、通知される場合があります。発信者は、リストされたすべての受信者が受け入れ可能である場合にのみ、MSP の処理とメッセージの送信を完了するよう、任意で要求できます。
contents.html: If multiple recipients are specified, access control checks (including calls to the PAA and PAE procedures) are performed for each recipient. A distinct EV governs message transfer to each recipient of a multicast message. If access control checks fail for some recipients of a multicast message, this need not preclude transmission of the message to those recipients for whom the checks succeed. An originator may (depending on local implementation and policy) be informed when one or more of a message's recipients are unacceptable for access control reasons. Optionally, an originator may request that MSP processing and message transmission be completed only if all listed recipients are acceptable.

contents.html_ja: 送信メッセージの場合のピアのセキュリティ情報の取得の機能は、メッセージ受信者の掲示された証明書、RandomPart、および AV（使用する場合）を MSP から取得する役割を担います（たとえば、必要になりうるディレクトリへの問い合わせを実行するのは MSP です）。メッセージ受信者の情報を取得する正確な方法と、メッセージ受信者の情報が伝えられる媒体は、ローカルの事項であり、ローカル構成情報の適用によって決定されます。（たとえば、受信者の情報は、ディレクトリサーバー、ローカルのキャッシュ、またはリモートのキャッシュに掲示されている場合があります。）メッセージ受信者の情報の取得の試みが成功すれば、Obtain_Peer_Info = Success となり、メッセージ受信者の情報が PAA の実行の機能に送られ、その機能が処理を実行します。
contents.html: The Obtain Peer Security Information On Outgoing Messages function is responsible for obtaining the message recipient's posted certificate, RandomPart, and AV (if used) from MSP (as an example it is MSP which will perform any directory queries which may be needed). The exact method for obtaining the message recipient's information and the medium on which the message recipient's information is conveyed is a local matter and will be determined through the application of local configuration information. (e.g., Recipient information may be posted on a directory server, in a local cache, or in a remote cache) If the attempt to obtain the message recipient information is successful, then Obtain_Peer_Info = Success and the message recipient's information is sent to the Perform PAA function so that it can perform its processing.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p71: 画像と語ごとに照合。節番号を見出しに戻し、下線（Obtain_Peer_Info）・節番号の空白・句読点を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: メッセージ受信者の情報の取得の試みが失敗すれば、Obtain_Peer_Info = Failure となり、通信は不可能です。メッセージ受信者の情報を取得できなかったことで、エラー状態が生成されますが、このエラー状態はアクセス制御の決定と解釈すべきではなく、通信の失敗です。処理の制御は MSP に戻されます。マルチキャストメッセージの場合、このエラー状態は、掲示された情報の取得を試みていた特定の受信者にのみ結び付けられます。
contents.html: If the attempt to obtain the message recipient's information is unsuccessful, then Obtain_Peer_Info = Failure and communications are impossible. The failure to obtain the message recipient's information results in the generation of an error condition, this error condition should not be construed as an access control decision but rather is a communications failure. Control of the processing is returned to MSP. In the case of a multicast message this error condition is only tied to the specific recipient for whom the attempt to retrieve posted information was being made.

All such information is available in the OriginatorSecurityData within the message's security heading. If the attempt to obtain the message's originator-specific information is successful, then Obtain_Peer_Info = Success and the message's originator-specific information is sent to the Perform PAA function so that it can perform its processing.

contents.html_ja: PAA の実行の機能の目的は、メッセージ発信者とメッセージ受信者の両方の Composite ID 情報を比較して、関連付けの基礎となりうる、共通に保持されるセキュリティ属性の集合が存在するかどうかを判定することです。PAA の手順では、UA が、ローカルの構成が定めるすべての PAA の機能を呼び出す役割を担います。PAA の詳細な説明については、第 4.1 節を参照してください。
contents.html: The purpose of the Perform PAA function is to compare both the message originator's and message recipient's Composite ID information to determine whether or not a commonly held set of security attributes exists on which an association can be based. In the PAA procedure, a UA is responsible for calling all the PAA functionality which the local configuration dictates. For a detailed description of PAA refer to section 4.1.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p72: 画像と語ごとに照合。節番号を見出しに戻し、入出力の項目を改行で分け、下線・句読点・段落の区切りを画像で直す。p73 に続く段落を含める

contents.html_ja: PAA が正常に完了すれば、PAA_Result = Pass となり、EV が PAE の実行の機能に渡され、その機能が処理を実行します。PAA が失敗すれば、PAA_Result = Fail となり、エラー状態が生成されます。PAA の失敗によって生成されるエラー状態は、2 つのピア間に許容される通信の組み合わせが存在しないことを示します。これはアクセス制御の決定です。送信マルチキャストメッセージの場合、このエラー状態は、PAA の実行を試みた特定の受信者にのみ結び付けられます。PAA が失敗した場合、処理の制御は、適切なエラー状態とともに MSP に戻されます。
contents.html: If PAA is successfully completed then PAA_Result = Pass, and the EV is passed to the Perform PAE function so that it can perform its processing. If the PAA is unsuccessful then PAA_Result = Fail and an error condition is generated. The error condition generated by a failed PAA would indicate that no allowable set of communications exists between the two peers, this is an access control decision. In the case of an outgoing multicast message, this error condition is only tied to the specific recipient for whom the attempt to perform PAA is made. If PAA fails, control of the processing is returned to the MSP along with the appropriate error condition.

contents.html_ja: PAE の実行の機能は、メッセージが EV に表される制約を満たすかどうかを判定します。発信側の UA では、RBAC の判定は、セキュリティに関連する属性を表す提出エンベロープのフィールド、または処理の文脈に基づいて暗黙的に決まるセキュリティ属性（あるいはその両方）に基づきます。受信側の UA では、RBAC の判定は、メッセージに含まれ、その受信者に対応する ProtectedToken 内の機微度の表示に基づきます。
contents.html: The Perform PAE function determines whether a message meets the constraints represented in an EV. At an originator UA, RBAC determinations are based on submission envelope fields representing security-relevant attributes and/or on security attributes determined implicitly based on processing context. At a recipient UA, RBAC determinations are based on the sensitivity indication carried within the ProtectedToken carried in the message and corresponding to that recipient.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p73: 画像と語ごとに照合。先頭の段落は p72 にまとめた。節番号を見出しに戻し、O/R・下線（PAE_Result）を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: 発信側での IBAC の実施は、メッセージの宛先である受信者の発信者/受信者（O/R）名の集合に基づき、これに対応して、受信側での IBAC の実施は、受信メッセージの originatorCertificate から取り出した発信者の O/R 名に基づくと想定します。IBAC チェックが（EV の確立を試みる際の）PAA 処理の過程で行われる場合、それらを PAE に組み込む必要はありません。
contents.html: It is assumed that IBAC enforcement at an originator is based on the set of recipient Originator/Recipient (O/R) names to whom a message is directed and, correspondingly, that IBAC enforcement at a recipient is based on the originator O/R name as extracted from the originatorCertificate in an incoming message. If the IBAC checks will be performed in the course of PAA processing (as EV establishment is attempted) they need not be incorporated within PAE.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p73: 画像と語ごとに照合。先頭の段落は p72 にまとめた。節番号を見出しに戻し、O/R・下線（PAE_Result）を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: PAE の機能が正常に完了すれば、PAE_Result = Pass となり、MSP への復帰の機能が呼び出されて処理を実行します。PAE の機能が失敗すれば、PAE_Result = Fail となり、エラー状態が生成されます。PAE の失敗によって生成されるエラー状態は、調べているメッセージが、PAA の間にその通信に対して確立された範囲に収まらなかったことを示し、これはアクセス制御の決定です。送信のマルチキャストメッセージの場合、このエラー状態は、PAE の実行を試みた特定の受信者にのみ結び付けられます。PAE が失敗した場合、処理の制御は、適切なエラー状態とともに MSP に戻されます。
contents.html: If the PAE function is successfully completed then PAE_Result = Pass, and the Return to MSP function is called to perform its processing. If the PAE function is unsuccessful then PAE_Result = Fail, and an error condition is generated. The error condition generated by a failed PAE would indicate that the message being examined did not fall within the bounds established for that communications during PAA, this is an access control decision. In the case of an outgoing multicast message, this error condition is only tied to the specific recipient for whom the attempt to perform PAE is made. If PAE fails, control of the processing is returned to the MSP along with the appropriate error condition.

contents.html_ja: アクセス制御情報仕様の必要性は、アクセス制御作業部会（ACWG）によるさまざまなパーティションの調査の結果として確立されました。このツールはすべてのパーティションに適用してもよいですが、すべてのパーティションのセキュリティ属性構造について、詳細な調査はまだ行われていません。
contents.html: The requirement for the Access Control Information Specification has been established as a result of the Access Control Working Group's (ACWG) investigation of various Partitions. This tool may be applied to all Partitions, but as yet a detailed investigation of the Security Attribute structures of all Partitions has not been made.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p75: 画像と語ごとに照合。節番号の見出しのレベルを直し、(a)〜(c) を番号付きの箇条にし、語順の崩れ（ACWG）・句読点・SDN.802/1 を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: 調査により、多くの環境のセキュリティ属性は、階層型でもあり非階層型でもあり、木構造で表現できることがわかりました。この編成方式は、このデータを主証明書または補助ベクトルで表現しようとする際に、いくつかの問題を生じさせました。データを階層に分け、1 つの階層全体を連続して表現してから次の階層に移ると、調べている現在の階層に下位階層の属性を関連付けようとする際に、曖昧さが生じる場合があります。一方、木の各枝を完全かつ独立に表現すると、あまりにも多くの容量が必要になります。さらに重要なことに、アクセス制御データを符号化し比較するための統一的な方法がなければ、多くの SDNS 実装が、各自のローカルのセキュリティポリシーに固有のソフトウェアを必要とすることがわかりました。これらの問題を解決するため、ACWG はアクセス制御情報仕様（ACIS）の開発に着手しました。
contents.html: Investigations have shown that the Security Attributes of many environments are both hierarchical and non-hierarchical in nature and can be represented as a tree structure. This organizational scheme posed some problems when trying to represent this data in a Primary Certificate or in an Auxiliary Vector. If the data is broken down into tiers and an entire tier is represented contiguously before moving to the next tier, ambiguities may arise when trying to associate lower tier attributes with the current tier being examined. On the other hand representing each branch of the tree completely and independently requires too much space. More importantly, it has been found that without some uniform method for encoding and comparing access control data many SDNS implementations would require software specific to their local security policy. With this set of issues to be resolved, the ACWG set out to develop the Access Control Information Specification (ACIS).

contents.html_ja: 5.1.1. ACIS に対するユーザー要件
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p76: 画像と語ごとに照合。句読点の脱落を画像で直す。p77 に続く段落を含める

contents.html_ja: ACIS は、特定のシステムのセキュリティ属性が一定の特性を持つ場合に生じる問題を扱うよう設計されています。これらの特性のうち最も重要なものは、システムのセキュリティ属性を、階層と相互依存を含意する木構造で表現できることです。システムの 2 つ目の特性は、そのアクセス制御が、通信を望む 2 つのエンティティの属性の共通部分を求めるプロセスとして実行できなければならないことです。
contents.html: ACIS is designed to handle problems that arise when the Security Attributes of a particular system have certain characteristics. The most important of these characteristics is that the system Security Attributes can be expressed in a tree structure, implying hierarchy and interdependence. A second characteristic of the system is that its access control must be able to be performed as an intersection process of the attributes of the two entities that wish to communicate.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p76: 画像と語ごとに照合。句読点の脱落を画像で直す。p77 に続く段落を含める

contents.html_ja: これらの特性に沿って、ACIS を使用する際に最初に行うタスクは、特定のパーティションのシステムセキュリティ属性の構造全体を木構造として表現することです。システムセキュリティ属性の木には、この属性の集合で通信が許可された場合にどのラベルが想定されるかを示す、PDU 属性の候補の集合を付加すべきです。図 5.1 と図 5.2 は、それぞれシステムの木と、許可されるラベルの集合を示しています。
contents.html: Consistent with these characteristics, the first task to accomplish when using ACIS is to express the entire System Security Attribute structure of a particular Partition as a tree structure. Appended to the System Security Attribute tree should be a collection of possible PDU attributes which indicate what label may be expected if communications is allowed for this set of attributes. Figures 5.1 and 5.2 show a system tree and a set of allowable labels, respectively.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p76: 画像と語ごとに照合。句読点の脱落を画像で直す。p77 に続く段落を含める

contents.html_ja: パーティション内では、通信する各エンティティが、システム全体のセキュリティ属性の一部を持つ場合があります。これらの各エンティティについて部分木を作成しなければならず、それはシステムの木と整合していなければなりません。さらに、通信を望む任意の 2 つのエンティティの表現（または部分木）は、通信が許可される各枝について、まったく同じ解釈を持たなければなりません。図 5.3 と図 5.4 は、図 5.1 のシステムの木から導出された、ホスト A とホスト B のサンプルの木を示しています。
contents.html: Within a Partition each communicating entity might have a subset of the overall System Security Attributes. A partial tree must be developed for each of these entities and it must be consistent with the system tree. Furthermore, the expressions (or partial trees) for any two entities that wish to communicate must have the exact same interpretation of each of the branches on which communications will be allowed. Figures 5.3 and 5.4 show a sample tree for Hosts A and B which has been derived from the system tree of Figure 5.1.

contents.html_ja: アクセス制御属性のこの予備的な編成と割り当ては、ACIS を機能させるうえで不可欠な部分であり、したがって、アクセス制御の正確な動作を確実にするために正しく行わなければなりません。この作業の大部分は、現在アクセス制御を採用するシステムで必要とされる予備的なタスクと整合しており、そのため、新たな作業が大幅に増えることはないはずです。
contents.html: This preliminary organization and assignment of access control attributes is an essential part of making ACIS work and must therefore be done correctly to insure the accurate performance of access control. For the most part this work is consistent with preliminary tasks required today for systems employing access control, and therefore should not introduce a significant amount of new work.

contents.html_ja: システムセキュリティ属性の木のどの部分を主証明書または補助ベクトル（あるいはその両方）に入れるかを決める際に、考慮すべき 2 つの場合があります。ACIS は、主証明書に置かれる情報には使用されないことに注意してください。フィールド間の相互関係は、補助ベクトルで表現されます。1 つ目の場合は、主として上で扱ったもので、4 階層モデルの 4 つの階層すべてにまたがる属性の集合全体に対して、単一の木がある場合です。この場合、すべての情報が主証明書に収まらなければ、補助ベクトルの木を完成させるために、主証明書の情報の一部を転送または複製する手段が必要になる場合があります。2 つ目に考慮すべき場合は、モデルの特定の階層の属性の各集合が、それ自体として別個の木である場合です。この場合、情報が主証明書に収まらなければ、情報を主証明書と補助ベクトルに分割しなければなりません。情報は分けられ、第 1 階層、第 2 階層、および第 4 階層の一部の情報は主証明書に、第 3 階層と第 4 階層の情報は補助ベクトルに置かれます。
contents.html: There are two cases to consider when deciding what portions of the System Security Attributes tree go into the Primary Certificate and/or the Auxiliary Vector. It should be noted that ACIS will not be used on any information placed in the primary certificate. Any interrelationships between any of the fields will be represented in the Auxiliary Vector. The first case, which is primarily the one addressed above, is when there is a single tree for the entire collection of attributes spanning all four tiers of the Four-Tiered Model. In this case, if all of the information cannot fit into the primary certificate a means for transferring or duplicating some primary certificate information may need to be done to complete the tree in the Auxiliary Vector. The second case to consider is when each set of the attributes for a particular tier in the model is a separate tree in and of itself. In this case, if the information cannot fit into the primary certificate then the information must be split between primary certificate and auxiliary vector. The information would be broken down; the Tier 1, Tier 2, and some Tier 4 information will be in the Primary Certificate and the Tier 3 and 4 information will be in the Auxiliary Vector.

contents.html_ja: ACIS は、いくつかの機能と文法で構成されています。前の図に見られるように、セキュリティ属性の相互関係を正確に表現するには、論理演算子が必要です。図には（例示のため）「and」と「or」の演算子が示されています。その他の演算子は、SDNS Access Control Specification, Addendum 1（SDN.802/1）、すなわち ACIS の詳細仕様で詳しく説明されています。各演算子には、固有の文字が対応付けられています。この演算子の集合とその表現が、ACIS の文法を構成します。この文法は、システムまたはエンティティ属性の木を構築する際に使用されます。
contents.html: ACIS is constructed of several functions and a grammar. As seen in the previous figures, logical operators are required in order to accurately express the interrelationships of Security Attributes. Shown in the figures (for the purpose of example) are the 'and' and 'or' operators. Other operators are detailed in the SDNS Access Control Specification, Addendum 1 (SDN.802/1); the ACIS Detailed Specification. Associated with each operator is a unique character. This set of operators and their representations comprise the ACIS grammar. This grammar is used when constructing the System or Entity Attribute tree.

contents.html_ja: ACIS の複数の機能のうち最初のものは、符号化機能です。このプロセスは、木構造の属性を入力として受け取り、それを、補助ベクトルの中に置ける連続した文字の集合として書き出します。この文字列は、アクセス制御式と呼ばれます。図 5.5 は、ホスト A と呼んだエンティティの符号化プロセスを示しています。逆に、連続したバイト列を入力として受け取り、システムまたはエンティティの木を再構築できる、復号機能があります。この概念は図 5.6 に示されています。
contents.html: The first of several functions of ACIS is the encoding function. The process takes the tree structured attributes as an input and writes it as a set of contiguous characters which can then be placed inside an auxiliary vector. This string is called an Access Control Expression. Figure 5.5 shows the encoding process of the Entity we called Host A. Conversely, there is a decoding function which takes as input a contiguous string of bytes and can reconstruct the System or Entity tree. This concept is shown in Figure 5.6.

contents.html_ja: PAA プロセスの間に、通信を望むエンティティのセキュリティ属性が交換されます。これら 2 つのエンティティに共通するセキュリティ属性があるかどうかを判定するには、共通部分を求める「比較」プロセスが行われなければなりません。ACIS の比較機能は、任意の 2 つの符号化された文字列を入力として受け取り、共通部分のない属性を除去します。2 つの共通部分にあたる領域は、PAE プロセスのための情報として EV に保存されます。PAE の処理一式がすべて関係するのは、明示的なラベル付けが使われ、かつラベルの値が関連付けの存続期間中に変化しうる場合だけであることに注意してください。どちらの文字列についても、共通部分にあたらない部分は除去（剪定）されます。共通部分が存在しない場合は、通信は許可されません。ACIS のこの比較機能は、許可された通信を保証するとともに、許可されていないラベルの除去を確実にしなければなりません。図 5.7 は、ホスト A とホスト B について、この剪定プロセスを概念的に示しています。
contents.html: During the PAA process the Security Attributes of the entities wishing to communicate are exchanged. In order to determine if these two entities have Security Attributes in common, an intersection or 'Comparison' process must take place. The Compare function in ACIS takes as input any two Encoded strings and eliminates the nonintersecting attributes. Areas where the two intersect are preserved as information in the EV for the PAE process. Note that the full suite of PAE is only relevant when explicit labeling is used and when label values may vary during the lifetime of an association. Those portions of either string which do not intersect are eliminated (pruned). In cases where no intersection exists the communication is disallowed. This Comparing function of ACIS must assure the elimination of unauthorized labels, as well as guarantee authorized communications. contents.html: If communications are permitted, continuous access control is affected by means of the PAE process. This process involves comparing a PDU’s attributes with the contents of an EV. When a path is found that is common to both parties, the end of that path should contain a set of allowable labels representing that path. When PAE is performed, the PDU’s attributes are compared with this set extracted from the EV.

contents.html_ja: 以下は、高水準のシナリオの例です。パーティションのセキュリティ担当者が、システムセキュリティ属性の木を構築します。以降のエンティティの木はすべて、これから導出されます。エンティティの代表者が、そのエンティティをシステムに登録したいとき、適切な書類が記入されます。発注の窓口（情報が別々の塊で運ばれる場合は 2 か所）で、情報がコンピュータシステムに入力され、そこで属性がチェックされ符号化されます。その結果得られるアクセス制御式は、補助ベクトルに入れられます。その後、属性は SDNS コンポーネントにロードされ、前の節で論じたピアアクセス承認とピアアクセス実施に従って、交換され、チェックされます。
contents.html: The following is an example of a high level scenario. The security officer for a partition will construct the System Security Attributes tree. From this all subsequent Entity trees will be derived. When an Entity's representative wants to enter that Entity into the system, the appropriate paperwork is filled out. At the ordering station/s (two if the information is carried in separate chunks) the information is entered into a computer system which checks and encodes the attributes. The resulting Access Control Expression is then entered into the Auxiliary Vector. The attributes are then loaded into the SDNS component and exchanged and checked as per Peer Access Approval and Peer Access Enforcement, discussed in the previous section.

contents.html: This function is composed of several activities. One of the activities is identifying the various access control attributes that are to be incorporated into the rule-based SDNS component enforcement policy. This task entails identifying those items out of all those which exist in the system to make a part of the SDNS RBAC enforcement. Some of the access control items which are appropriate for access control at a user level, for example, may not be appropriate for use by a network level SDNS device. During the process it is important to keep in mind the restrictions imposed by the SDNS ACIS supported mechanisms. These will be discussed in section 2.2. Identification of the access control items includes defining the allowable values that these items can assume and any relationships that exist between items. It is possible, that some items may be redundant so that not including them in the SDNS rule-based enforcement will not result in any loss of enforcement functionality.

contents.html_ja: 次に、PAA と PAE の情報からなる文法が構築されます。文法の PAA 部分は、2 つの加入者エンティティ間の通信を認可するために PAA プロセスで使用されるアクセス制御属性を表します。PAE 文法は、PDU ラベルで使用され、PAE の間に実施ベクトルによってテストされる項目のみを表します。文法のこれらの部分が議論の中で別々に識別されているのは、2 つの加入者エンティティ間の通信を認可するために実施式で表現されるアクセス制御属性（PAA）が、通信が認可された後に PDU ラベルで運ばれる属性（PAE）とは、異なる可能性が非常に高いからです。たとえば、加入者エンティティの COMPUSEC 認証レベルは、2 つの加入者エンティティが通信できるかどうかを判定するポリシーの一部にはなりえますが、通信が認可された後に PDU ラベルで運ぶには、おそらく適切ではありません。PAE のラベル付け情報も、PAA 情報の拡張である可能性がかなり高く、すなわち、PAA の属性が、適切な PDU ラベルの値を決定することになります。
contents.html: Next a grammar consisting of PAA and PAE information is constructed. The PAA portion of the grammar represents access control attributes that are used during the PAA process to authorize communication between two subscriber entities. The PAE grammar represents only those items which are used in PDU labels and which are tested by the enforcement vector during PAE. These portions of the grammar are separately identified in the discussion because the access control attributes that are represented in an enforcement expression to authorize communication between two subscriber entities (PAA) are very likely different than the attributes that are carried in PDU labels after communication has been authorized (PAE). For example, the COMPUSEC Certification level of a subscriber entity may be part of a policy to determine whether two subscriber entities may communicate but would probably not be appropriate to carry in a PDU label after communication is authorized. The PAE labelling information is also quite likely an extension of the PAA information, i.e., the PAA attributes will dictate the appropriate PDU label values.

contents.html: ACIS uses the concept of parse trees and predictive parsers in order to test PDU labels and to compare access attributes in PAA. However, unlike the theoretical treatment in Section 6, ACIS does not require that parse trees be constructed dynamically to test PDU labels. Instead, a single parse tree representing all acceptable PDU labels for the system is constructed at the time the access control policy representation is generated. This single parse tree is the system attribute tree. Also contained in the attribute tree is access control information used during PAA. Part of the tree generation task is to guarantee that the representation is unambiguous and suitable for use as a predictive parser for label testing.

contents.html: The AND and the OR operators can be thought of as the fundamental operations that are defined for use in productions. All of the productions supported by ACIS can be defined in terms of these two basic operations. In some cases though, the definition process may be somewhat cumbersome because of the potentially large list of symbols which would be required to be used in productions to represent some relationships. To combat this problem and to provide a slightly higher level of abstraction, the following operators have been defined.

contents.html: The bit vector range can be used as a more economical representation method of defining set membership than by explicitly identifying each member of the set. Potentially bit vectors could be used when the number of members that can be identified in a label becomes comparable with the set size. For example, suppose that there are eight members in a set and that potentially all of them could be named within a label. If the members of the set are identified in three bits and each of the members was explicitly named, it would take 8 * 3 bits = 24 bits to list all of the members. However if each member was assigned a particular bit position then naming all eight members takes only 8 bits. The presence of a 1 in a particular bit position reflects the presence of that member in the label while a 0 reflects its absence. The overhead associated with the bit vector is always 8 bits even if the list is empty whereas an explicit list would require zero bits to represent an empty list. The bit vector range representation however, does not allow the same degree of granularity as the list since it is impossible to exclude particular members falling within the range.
contents.html_ja: ビットベクトル範囲は、集合のメンバーを1つずつ明示的に識別するよりも効率的に、集合への所属を定義する表現方法として使えます。ラベル内で識別できるメンバー数が集合の大きさに近い場合、ビットベクトルを使える可能性があります。たとえば、集合に8つのメンバーがあり、そのすべてをラベル内で指定するとします。集合の各メンバーが3ビットで表され、各メンバーを明示的に指定した場合、すべてのメンバーを列挙するには 8 * 3 ビット = 24 ビットが必要になります。しかし、各メンバーに特定のビット位置を割り当てれば、8つすべてのメンバーを指定するのに必要なのは8ビットだけです。特定のビット位置に1があれば、そのメンバーがラベルに含まれることを示し、0は含まれないことを示します。ビットベクトルに伴うオーバーヘッドは、リストが空であっても常に8ビットですが、明示的なリストでは空のリストを表すのに0ビットで済みます。ただし、ビットベクトル範囲による表現は、範囲内の特定のメンバーを除外できないため、リストと同じ粒度にはできません。

contents.html_ja: この演算子は、COMPUSEC の支配関係を表現するためにも使えます。上限値は下限値を支配するとされます。上限値は、認可される項目の最大数を示します。1 のビットは、そのカテゴリに対する認可を示します。下限値は、ラベル内で識別しなければならない項目の最小数を示します。最小数の項目が識別され、認可されていない項目が一つも識別されない限り、そのラベルは受け入れ可能です。
contents.html: This operator can also be used to express a COMPUSEC dominance relationship. The upper value is said to dominate the lower value. The upper limit identifies the maximum number of items that are authorized. A 1 bit identifies authorization for that category. The lower value identifies the minimum number of items that must be identified in a label. So long as the minimum number of items are identified and as long as none are identified that are not authorized the label is acceptable.

contents.html: The value of the range expression can be derived by performing a bitwise-and of the two values and by setting those bit positions that are a "one" in the upper limit and a "zero" in the lower limit to a don’t-care (represented by an x). This means that either value in that bit position is valid. Thus, for the example cited, the resulting range of acceptable values when expressed in binary form is (0XXX0010). This range is explicitly listed in the expanded production.

contents.html: The grammar is represented as a tree in Figure 2.2.3-1. The nodes have been numbered to ease the discussion. The process basically consists of identifying the first character beginning each string and seeing if two alternate choices begin with the same first character. The process begins at the leafs. At node 8, for example, the first character that could be generated at this node is x. This set of characters is denoted by (x) shown beside the node. At node 10, the first character of a possible string begins with R. At node 6, any value is acceptable because the node is a don’t care operator. Travelling up the tree there are two cases to consider. If the operator is an OR, the first character set becomes the union of the nodes immediately below it. Thus at node 4, the set is composed of X and Y. If the operator is an AND, the first set is becomes the first set of the leftmost subnode since subnodes to the right of this node cannot begin the string. Thus at node 2 the set is composed of (X, Y). Preceding up to node 1, we see there is an ambiguity since the first characters from node 2 are X any Y and these same characters are included from the don’t care values from node 3.

contents.html_ja: 現状の生成規則は、B から導出される文字列が X または Y のいずれかで始まり、C から導出される文字列が X や Y を含む任意の値で始まりうるため、受け入れられません。これは、A に関連付けられた生成規則が曖昧であることを意味します。この曖昧さを解消するには、C の生成規則の DONT_CARE フィールドの前に、X でも Y でもない終端記号を追加できます。たとえば、生成規則を C → F + DONT_CARE(1) + Q に変更すれば、曖昧さは解消されます。非終端記号 B を使う文字列は X または Y で始まり、非終端記号 C から導出される文字列は F で始まります。
contents.html: As the productions currently stand they are unacceptable because the strings derived from B begin with either X or Y and the strings derived from C may begin with any value including X or Y. This means that the production associated with A is ambiguous. To resolve the ambiguity, a terminal other than X or Y can be added before the DONT_CARE field in the production for C. For example, if the production is changed to C → F + DONT_CARE(1) + Q, the ambiguity is resolved. Strings using the nonterminal B begin with X or Y while the the strings derived from nonterminal C begin with F.

contents.html: The tree graphically represents the acceptable PDU labels per the policy representation. There are two acceptable labels defined for this system. The first is the basic option which is indicated by a 82H appearing as the first character of the label. The second is the extended security option which is indicated by a starting character of 85H. contents.html_ja: 特定の加入者エンティティに対するパーティションアクセス制御順序を生成するために、Partition Order Forms、Local Domain Authority Identifier、Partition Ordering Restrictions、および加入者（エンティティ）のパーティションアクセス制御属性が使用されます。Partition Order Forms は、パーティションについて定義された可能な属性全体のうち、特定の加入者エンティティに関連するさまざまなアクセス制御属性を入れるテンプレートを提供します。基本的に、このプロセスは、パーティション内に存在するアクセス制御属性を特定の加入者エンティティ向けにカスタマイズすることから成ります。Partition Order Restrictions（存在する場合）は、User Representative（UR）が Partition Ordering Forms に入れることを許されるアクセス制御属性に何らかの制限があるかどうかを決定します。Local Domain Authority ID は、ローカルアクセス制御システムをサポートするために必要となる任意の情報です。Local Domain Authority ID は、ローカルアクセス制御情報を含む Auxiliary Vector（AV）を生成できる、認可された Local Authority を識別します。基本的に、補助ベクトルの情報は、AV を生成した主体（すなわち Local Domain Authority）が primary certificate で識別されているため、真正であると信頼できます。Local Authority には Message Signature Key が関連付けられています。この鍵は、補助ベクトルの完全性を確保するデジタル署名を生成するために使用されます。
contents.html: Partition Ordering Forms, Local Domain Authority Identifier, Partition Ordering Restrictions, and the subscriber (entity) partition access control attributes are used to generate a partition access control order for a particular subscriber entity. The Partition Order Forms provide a template into which are placed the various access control attributes relevant to a particular subscriber entity out of the total set of possible attributes which were defined for the partition. Essentially this process consists of customizing the access control attributes that exist within a partition to a particular subscriber entity. The Partition Order Restrictions (if there are any) determine whether there are any restrictions upon what access control attributes a User Representative (UR) is allowed to place in the Partition Ordering Forms. The Local Domain Authority ID is optional information which is required to support the local access control system. The Local Domain Authority ID identifies the authorized Local Authority which is able to generate Auxiliary Vectors (AVs) containing local access control information. Essentially the information in an auxiliary vector can be believed to be authentic because the agent that generated the AV (i.e., the Local Domain Authority) was identified in the primary certificate. Associated with the Local Authority is a Message Signature Key. This key is used to generate a digital signature which ensures the integrity of the auxiliary vector.

contents.html_ja: AV は主に、ローカルアクセス制御ポリシー情報を SDNS コンポーネントに配布する手段として使われます。これには、ルールベースとアイデンティティベースの両方のアクセス制御情報が含まれます。このプロセスはローカル機関の管理下にあるため、ポリシー表現にはより大きなばらつきが予想されます。加えて、これは厳密にローカルの事項であるため、AV に追加情報を含めることもできます。ただし、ローカルのルールベースポリシーレベルで相互運用性を確保するため、ルールベースのローカルアクセス制御情報は ACIS 形式で表現されるものと想定されています。
contents.html: The AV is used mostly as a vehicle for distributing local access control policy information to the SDNS component. This includes both rule-based and identity-based access control information. Because this process is under a local authority's control, greater variation is expected in the policy expression. In addition, it is possible for the AV to contain additional information since this is strictly a local concern. It is assumed, however, that the rule-based local access control information will be represented in an ACIS format to ensure interoperability at local rule-based policy level.

contents.html_ja: 以下の符号化規則は、NBS.1 ASN.1 の方法論に似せて設計されています。この方法は、すべてのデータフィールドの前に型フィールドと長さフィールドを付けることで構成されます。この方式は容易に拡張でき、実際のデータ形式に制限を課しません。型フィールドは、データフィールド内のデータの型（整数やオクテット列など）を識別します。長さフィールドはデータのバイト単位の長さを指定し、データフィールドには実際のデータが含まれます。標準 ASN.1 定義では、型フィールドと長さフィールドはそれぞれ少なくとも 1 バイトと規定されています。
contents.html: The following encoding rules have been designed to resemble the NBS.1 ASN.1 methodology. This method consists of preceding all data fields with type and length fields. This approach is easily expandable and places no restrictions on the format of the actual data. The type field identifies the type of data within the data field, such as integer or octetstring. The length field specifies the length in bytes of the data and the data field contains the actual data. The standard ASN.1 definition specifies the type and length fields to be at least one byte each.

contents.html_ja: エンティティ属性の木の符号化に使われるバイト数は重大であるため、ASN.1 の方法は、型フィールドと長さフィールドに必要なバイト数を減らすように修正されています。これは、型識別子と、型フィールドおよび長さフィールドの長さを再定義することで達成されます。データ型はすべて 1 ニブルで定義され、可能な限り、データ長フィールドは次のニブルに符号化されます（データの長さが < 16 バイトの場合）。これにより、AV 内で型フィールドと長さフィールドを符号化するのに必要なバイト数は、標準の ASN.1 符号化に比べて半分になります。
contents.html: Since the number of bytes used to encode the entity attribute trees is critical, the ASN.1 approach has been modified to reduce the number of bytes necessary for the type and length fields. This is achieved by redefining the type identifiers and lengths of the type and length fields. The data types are all defined by one nibble and wherever possible the data length field is encoded in the following nibble (if the length of data is < 16 bytes). This reduces by half the number of bytes necessary to encode the type and length fields in the AV over the standard ASN.1 encoding.

contents.html_ja: 制御データフィールドは、葉ノード以外のノードを表す制御文字を符号化するために使われます。これらの制御ノードは、データを含む場合があり（その場合は E または 0 の型フィールド指示子を用いて符号化されます）、含まない場合もあります（その場合は F の型フィールド指示子を用いて符号化されます）。制御データ型フィールドを用いて符号化されるデータの例は、「OR」または「AND」ノードです。制御文字は 1 ニブルの長さと定義されており、可能な場合は複数の制御文字を 1 つのデータフィールド内にまとめて配置します。制御文字の数が奇数の場合は、データフィールド内の残りのバイトを埋めるためにヌル文字が使われます。
contents.html: The control data field is used to encode control characters which represent nodes other than leaf nodes. These leaf nodes may contain data (in which case they would be encoded using an E or 0 type field indicator) or may not (in which case they would be encoded using an F type field indicator). Examples of data encoded using a Control Data type field are an "OR" or an "AND" node. The control characters are defined to be one nibble long and where possible multiple control characters are placed together within a single data field. If there are an odd number of of control characters then a null character is used to pad the remainder of the byte within the data field.

contents.html_ja: 制御データフィールドの前には、上位ニブルに制御データ型指示子（16 進の D）を、下位ニブルに制御データの長さ（バイト単位）の表示を含む、1 バイトが付きます。これにより、データフィールドに最大 15 バイト、すなわち 30 個の制御文字を表現できます。より多くの制御ノードを表現する場合は、2 つ目の制御データフィールドの表現を、前の制御フィールドの符号化に連結できます。制御データフィールドで使用される制御文字の定義を、以下に示します。16 進の 6 から E の値は、ACIS に今後定義される可能性のある演算子を表すために使用できます。値 F は、木の中の実際のノードには対応せず、符号化された表現から木を生成するプロセスの間の制御情報に使われます。その使い方は、後で説明します。
contents.html: Control Data fields are preceded by a byte containing a Control Data type indicator (D hex) in the upper nibble and a indication of length of the control data (in bytes) in the low order nibble. This allows a maximum of 15 bytes or 30 control characters to be represented in the datafield. If a greater number of control nodes are to be represented, a second control data field representation can be concatenated to the previous control field encoding. The definitions of the control characters used in the control data field are shown below. The values 6 through E hex can be used to represent future operators that may defined for ACIS. The value F does not actually correspond to any actual node within a tree but is used rather for control information during the process of generating a tree from its encoded representation. Its use will be illustrated later.

contents.html_ja: 葉データフィールドは、葉ノードに置かれるデータを含みます。「Leaf」ノードを示す特別な制御文字は定義されていません。葉データフィールドに遭遇したときは常に、葉データを格納するために LEAF ノードを作成する必要があるため、「Leaf」ノードを示す必要はありません。制御データフィールドと同様に、データフィールドの前には、上位ニブルに葉データ型を、下位ニブルに葉データの長さを含む 1 バイトが付きます。ただし、葉データが 15 バイトを超える場合は、葉データ型を下位ニブルに置き、上位ニブルは ZERO に設定します。その場合、葉データの長さは次のバイトに符号化されます。この符号化は、葉データが 255 バイトを超えることはないと想定しています。
contents.html: The leaf data field contains data to be placed into a leaf node. A special control character has not been defined to indicate a "Leaf" node. It is not necessary to indicate a "Leaf" node since whenever a leaf data field is encountered it is necessary to create a LEAF node to store the leaf data. As with the control data field, the data field is preceded by a byte containing the leaf data type in the high order nibble and the length of the leaf data in the low order nibble. However, if the leaf data is longer that 15 bytes then the leaf data type is placed in the low order nibble with the high order nibble set equal to ZERO. The length of the leaf data is then encoded within the next byte. This encoding assumes leaf data will never be greater than 255 bytes.

For example the two range operators (the numeric and bit vector range) have an indication of the upper and lower range values. This control information will be encoded in leaf nodes associated with the particular operator. Thus, for the examples just cited, each of the range operator nodes would have two leaf nodes below the range node to indicate the top and bottom of the range. There is also control information associated with the N_OF operator.

contents.html: The control buffer and the AV buffer are global structures which need to be initialized before the start of the transformation. The control buffer is used for the temporary storage of control characters before they are encoded into a control data field. The AV buffer is used to build the AV string a segment at a time. A segment consists of type, length and data fields. When the transformation is complete the AV buffer contains the completely encoded AV string.
contents.html_ja: 制御バッファと AV バッファは、変換の開始前に初期化する必要があるグローバルな構造です。制御バッファは、制御文字が制御データフィールドに符号化される前に、一時的に格納するために使われます。AV バッファは、AV 文字列を 1 セグメントずつ構築するために使われます。セグメントは、型、長さ、データの各フィールドで構成されます。変換が完了すると、AV バッファには、完全に符号化された AV 文字列が入っています。

contents.html_ja: 木の符号化の関数は、最初に根ノードを引数として呼び出され、その後、すべての下位ノードが処理されるまで、各下位ノードについて自分自身を再帰的に呼び出します。親ノードの下位ノードはどれも、親に戻る前に、可能な限り下位の子ノード（LEAF）まで処理されます。木を下るために必要な制御文字は、LEAF ノードに到達するまで制御バッファに保存されます。LEAF ノードに到達すると、制御バッファ内の制御文字が（前に型フィールドと長さフィールドを付けて）制御データフィールドに符号化され、AV バッファに追加されます。その後、制御バッファはクリアされます。次に、LEAF データが LEAF データフィールドに符号化され、AV バッファに追加されます。LEAF データが AV に追加された後、木の符号化の関数は LEAF ノードの親に戻り、さらに下位ノードがないかをチェックします。再帰的な木の符号化の関数は、終了するたびに、（処理中のノードのすぐ上の）親ノードに戻り、最終的に根ノードに到達して完了します。
contents.html: The encode tree function is initially invoked with the root node, and then calls itself recursively for each subnode until all subnodes have been processed. Each and every subnode of a parent node is processed to the lowest possible child node (a LEAF) before returning to the parent. The control characters necessary to descend down the tree are saved in the control buffer until a LEAF node is reached. When a LEAF node is reached the control characters in the control buffer are encoded into a control data field (with preceding type and length fields) and are added to the AV buffer. The control buffer is then cleared. Next, the LEAF data is encoded into a LEAF data field and added to the AV buffer. After the LEAF data is added to the AV then the encode tree function returns to the parent of the LEAF node and checks for more subnodes. Each time the recursive encode tree function ends, it returns to the parent node (immediately above the node being processed) until it finally reaches the root node and is complete.

contents.html_ja: AV 文字列は、制御データと葉データの連続したセグメントを含みます。文字列は、末尾に到達するまで 1 セグメントずつ処理されます。各セグメントは、型、長さ、データの各フィールドを含みます。型フィールドと長さフィールドは、データフィールドの記述子です。
contents.html: The AV string contains consecutive segments of control and leaf data. The string is processed a segment at a time until the end of the string is reached. Each segment contains a type, length and data field. The type and length fields are descriptors of the data field.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p128: 画像と語ごとに照合。節番号 3.2.4、ACI5→ACIS、Indicate→indicate、引用符を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: セグメントの最初のフィールドは型フィールドで、データフィールド内のデータの型を識別します。セグメントの 2 番目のフィールドは長さフィールドで、データフィールド内のデータのバイト数を指定します。データの長さが 16 バイト未満の場合、型フィールドと長さフィールドは同じバイトに置かれます。そうでない場合、型フィールドと長さフィールドは連続するバイトに置かれます。
contents.html: The first field of the segment is the type field and it identifies the type of data within the data field. The second field of the segment is the length field which specifies the number of bytes of data within the data field. When the length of the data is less than 16 bytes the type and length fields are placed in the same byte. Otherwise, the type and length fields are placed in consecutive bytes.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p128: 画像と語ごとに照合。節番号 3.2.4、ACI5→ACIS、Indicate→indicate、引用符を画像で直す

contents.html_ja: 型フィールドは、データフィールド内のデータの用い方も規定します。制御データ型は、データフィールドを 1 ニブルずつ処理し、各ニブルが（上で定義した）制御文字を表すことを指定します。制御文字がノードの作成を指定するたびに、そのノードが初期化され、既存のノードに接続されます。新しいノードは親ノードとみなされ、次の制御文字は新しいノードに関連付けられます。木を下る間にノードのポインタを保存するために、後入れ先出し（LIFO）キューが使われます。したがって、制御文字がノードの作成を指定するたびに、親ノードへのポインタが LIFO にプッシュされます。木を上るには、親ノードへのポインタを LIFO からポップします。これは、後戻り制御文字を定義することで実装されます。後戻り制御文字は、ノードのポインタを LIFO キューからポップすることを指定します。後続の制御文字は、ポップされたノードに関連付けられます。
contents.html: The type field also dictates the utilization of the data within the data field. The control data type specifies that the data field is to be processed a nibble at a time with each nibble representing a control character (as defined above). Each time a control character specifies the creation of a node, the node is initialized and attached to the previously existing node. The new node is now considered the parent node and the next control character is associated with the new node. A Last In First Out (LIFO) queue is used to save the node pointers while descending down the tree. Accordingly, each time a control character specifies the creation of a node, a pointer to the parent node is pushed onto the LIFO. The tree is ascended by popping a pointer to the parent node off of the LIFO. This is implemented by defining a backup control character. A backup control character specifies to pop a node pointer off of the LIFO queue. Subsequent control characters are then associated with the popped node.

contents.html_ja: 木の中の階層の変化は、制御データを処理するときにのみ起こります。葉フィールドと Don't Care フィールドは、単に LEAF ノードを作成し、葉データをそのノードに格納し、その LEAF ノードを現在のノードに接続することを指定します。木の中の階層は変化しません。これにより、追加の制御データなしに、1 つの親の下に複数の LEAF ノードを置けます。木の中の階層が変わるのは、制御データフィールドで「F」に遭遇したときだけです。この制御文字は、アルゴリズムが現在のノードの親に「後戻り」すべきことを示すために使われます。
contents.html: The changing of levels in a tree only occurs when processing control data. Leaf and Don't Care fields simply specify to create a LEAF node, store the leaf data to the node and attach the LEAF node to the present node. The level in the tree does not change. This allows multiple LEAF nodes to be placed below a single parent without additional control data. The level in a tree is only changed when "F" in a control data field is encountered. This control character is used to indicate that the algorithm should "back up" to the parent of the current node.

contents.html_ja: 開始側は、通信を確立したいとき、まず自身のローカルのエンティティ属性の木（エンティティの補助ベクトルに含まれています）を取得し、通信したい相手のリモートエンティティに送ります。リモートエンティティは、開始側の属性の木を受け取る（リモートエンティティ属性の木の受信）と、自身の属性の木の写しを取得して、開始側に送ります。
contents.html: When the initiator desires to establish communication it first obtains its own local entity attribute tree (which is contained in the entity's auxiliary vector) and sends it to the remote entity with whom communication is desired. When the remote entity receives the initiator's attribute tree (Receive Remote Entity Attribute Tree) it gets a copy of its own attribute tree and sends it to the initiator.

contents.html_ja: リモートエンティティの属性の木の受信には、AV の完全性と真正性を確実にするために必要な処理が伴います。この処理には、AV に使われている署名の検証と、ローカルドメイン機関が認可された機関であることのチェックが含まれます。その処理に加えて、補助ベクトルから RBAC と IBAC に関連する情報を取り出すために必要な処理があります。属性の木は、補助ベクトルに置くために何らかの形で符号化されなければならないため、属性の木を復元するには、符号化プロセスを元に戻す必要があります。RBAC と IBAC の情報を取り出すための要件、および符号化プロセスを元に戻して属性の木を復元することに関連する要件は、まだ示されていません。
contents.html: Associated with receiving a remote entity's attribute tree is processing required to ensure the integrity and authenticity of the AV. This process includes verifying the signature used on the AV and checking that the Local Domain Authority is an authorized authority. In addition to that processing is processing which is necessary to extract the RBAC and IBAC relevant information from the auxiliary vector. Since the attribute tree has to be encoded in some fashion in order to place it into the auxiliary vector, it is necessary to undo the encoding process to recover the attribute tree. The requirements for extracting the RBAC and IBAC information and those associated with undoing the encoding process to recover the attribute tree still need to be supplied.

contents.html: Once the remote and local attribute trees are obtained the Intersect Local and Remote Entity Attribute Trees function depicted in Figure 4-2 is invoked. A copy of the local attribute tree is passed to this function. This copy of the local attribute tree serves as the basis of comparison with the remote entity attribute tree. If the intersection is non-null, it will also become the PDU labelling testing portion of the EV. The intersection function returns a indication of whether the intersection process yields a non-null intersection. If a non-null result is obtained then communication is authorized and the resulting EV is stored for later use when testing PDU labels. If a null intersection results then it is necessary to perform the necessary error handling.
contents.html_ja: リモートとローカルの属性の木が得られると、図 4-2 に示すローカルとリモートのエンティティ属性の木の共通部分を求める機能が呼び出されます。ローカルの属性の木の写しが、この機能に渡されます。この写しは、リモートエンティティの属性の木との比較の基礎として機能します。共通部分が空でなければ、それは EV の PDU ラベルをテストする部分にもなります。共通部分を求める機能は、共通部分を求めるプロセスの結果が空でないかどうかを示す値を返します。空でない結果が得られれば、通信は認可され、得られた EV は、後で PDU ラベルをテストするときに使うために保存されます。空の共通部分になった場合は、必要なエラー処理を行う必要があります。

contents.html: Next a decision is made whether a PDU label test is necessary. This is done because not all PDUs need to contain PDU security labels (e.g., single-level hosts need not label). If a label test is not required, the RBAC portion of PAE is complete.

contents.html: If label testing is required, then the security label of the PDU (actually a pointer to the security label and the EV generated during PAA are retrieved (actually a pointer to the EV). The security label testing function is then invoked with the security label and the EV. The PDU security label testing function which is shown in Figures 5-2 through 5-10 then determine if the label matches the labelling requirements expressed in the EV. If the label passes the label testing then the PDU is authorized with respect to the ACIS RBAC rules and this part of the PAE process is complete. If the label is unacceptable then appropriate error handling of the PDU is required. This error handling may include destroying the PDU and auditing the event.
contents.html_ja: ラベルのテストが必要な場合は、PDU のセキュリティラベル（実際にはセキュリティラベルへのポインタ）と、PAA の間に生成された EV（実際には EV へのポインタ）が取得されます。その後、セキュリティラベルと EV を引数として、セキュリティラベルのテスト機能が呼び出されます。図 5-2 から図 5-10 に示す PDU セキュリティラベルテスト機能は、ラベルが EV で表現されたラベル付け要件に一致するかどうかを判定します。ラベルテストに合格すれば、その PDU は ACIS の RBAC ルールに関して認可され、PAE プロセスのこの部分は完了です。ラベルが受け入れられない場合は、その PDU に対する適切なエラー処理が必要です。このエラー処理には、PDU の破棄とイベントの監査が含まれる場合があります。

contents.html_ja: 終端記号は、言語の文が形成される最も基本的な記号です。「トークン」という語は「終端記号」の同義語です。トークンは、プログラミング言語に対して定義された文字のアルファベット（たとえば、A-Z a-z 0-9 ( ) , ; .）から取られた、何らかの意味のある文字列を表します。トークンは言語に対して定義される最下位の要素を構成するため、終端記号と呼ばれます。言語内の他のすべては、これらから構成されます。プログラミング言語のコンパイラでは、文字列 BEGIN や、（代入演算子として使われる）文字列「:=」にトークンが割り当てられる場合があります。ACIS では、終端記号によって、PDU ラベルに見られる実際の値や、何らかの基本的なアクセス制御属性などの要素が定義されます。
contents.html: Terminals are the most basic symbols from which sentences in a language are formed. The word "token" is a synonym for "terminal". Tokens represent some meaningful string of characters drawn from the alphabet of characters (e.g., A-Z a-z 0-9 ( ) , ; .) defined for the programming language. They constitute the lowest level elements defined for a language hence, the name terminal. Everything else in the language must be constructed from them. For a programming language compiler a token might be assigned to the character string BEGIN, or the character string ":=" (used as an assignment operator). For ACIS, the terminals define such elements as the actual values to be found in PDU labels or some elemental access control attribute.

contents.html_ja: 最後に、文法は生成規則で構成されます。生成規則は、終端記号と非終端記号を組み合わせて、言語内の終端文字列を形成する方法を指定します。生成規則は、生成規則の左辺と呼ばれる非終端記号、矢印（ → ）、およびトークンや非終端記号（あるいはその両方）の並びで構成されます。この終端記号や非終端記号（あるいはその両方）の並びは、生成規則の右辺と呼ばれます。→ は、生成規則の右辺が左辺の非終端記号の定義を与えることを示します。終端記号も非終端記号も含まない文字列を定義することも可能です。この文字列は空文字列と呼ばれ、e で表されます。表記上の便宜のため、左辺に同じ非終端記号を持つ生成規則は、代替の右辺を | 記号で区切ってまとめて書くことができます。この記号は「or」と読みます。
contents.html: Lastly, a grammar is composed of productions. These specify the manner in which the terminals and nonterminals can be combined to form terminal strings within the language. A production consists of a nonterminal, called the left side of the production, an arrow ( → ), and a sequence of tokens and/or nonterminals. This sequence of terminals and/or nonterminals is called the right side of the production. The → is used to indicate that the right side provides a definition for the nonterminal on the left side of the production. It is possible to define a string containing neither terminals nor nonterminals. This string is called the empty string and is denoted by e. For notational convenience, productions with the same nonterminal on the left side can have their right sides grouped with the alternative right sides separated by a | symbol. This symbol is read as an "or".

Left-recursion occurs when the nonterminal being defined also appears as the first (or leftmost) symbol on the right side of the production. For example consider the production A → Aa | b. The parse tree for the string baaaaa is shown in Figure 6.3-1. This production is left recursive because the nonterminal A appears as the leftmost symbol in the definition of the nonterminal A.

contents.html_ja: 構文解析のアルゴリズムには、基本的に 2 種類あります。トップダウンとボトムアップです。これらは、構文木のノードを構築する方法を指します。トップダウン法では、構築は開始の非終端記号を用いた根から始まり、葉（すなわち、終端記号またはトークンに向かって下）へ進みます。ボトムアップ構文解析では、構築は葉から始まり、根（すなわち、開始の非終端記号に向かって上）へ進みます。
contents.html: There are basically two kinds of parsing algorithms. They are top-down or bottom-up. These refer to the way in which nodes in the parse tree are constructed. In the top-down methods, construction begins with the root using the starting nonterminal and proceeding towards the leaves (i.e., down toward the terminals or tokens). In bottom up parsing, construction begins with the leaves and proceeds upward toward the root (i.e., up toward the starting nonterminal).

contents.html: The root of the parse tree is constructed using the starting nonterminal, type. This is shown in the first part of Figure 6.4-1. Since type is a nonterminal, it is necessary per step 1 of the algorithm to select one of the productions for type and construct children corresponding to each of the symbols on the right side of that production. In this example there are three possible choices that could be made for the definition of type. It could be defined by the nonterminal A, by the terminal a, or the terminal b followed by the nonterminal A followed by the terminal c. In order to determine which production should be selected, the terminal string being tested is used. This is done by scanning the token string in a left to right manner. The vertical arrow will be used to indicate the next character to be scanned and is called the lookahead symbol. In this example, it is clear that the production, type → b A c, is the correct choice because it is the only production that allows the token string to begin with the token b.

After using the symbol x in the token string, the lookahead symbol is advanced to the symbol c. This will be used to test the third child in the definition of type. Since the symbol in the parse tree and the symbol in the token string match (i.e., they are both c) and because this is the last child, the parse tree is complete. The lookahead symbol was advanced beyond the c to ensure that the token string contained no other characters to be parsed. Notice that the token string to be parsed can be found at the leaves of the parse tree. Since a parse tree could be generated for the token string, bxc is shown to be a valid string in the language defined by grammar2. If it had been impossible to generate such a parse tree, then the token string would have been declared invalid.

contents.html: In the example just presented it was straightforward to determine which production to select when constructing the parse tree using the lookahead symbol. For example, the only variable production for type was type → b A c. This was because it is the only production that allows for a token string to begin with b. If our grammar had also included the production type → b A d. Either production could have been selected when using only the lookahead symbol b. Each production will also work with the second symbol x. It is not until the lookahead symbol is advanced to the third (in this case c) that the correct choice can be determined. Thus if we had chosen the second production (type → b A d), it isn't until we test the third child d that we determine that this does not match the token string under test. At this point in order to pick the alternate production it is necessary to reset the lookahead symbol to b and to replace the incorrect node definition of type with the correct one, type b A c.

contents.html_ja: 一般に、生成規則の選択プロセスには試行錯誤が伴う場合があります。構文木を正常に定義できない生成規則を選択した場合は、構文木が構築されるか、すべての可能性が尽きるまで、バックトラックして別の生成規則を選択する必要があります。ただし、バックトラックが不要な特別なクラスの文法があります。これらの文法には、構文木を構築するときに選択する生成規則について曖昧さが生じないという特徴があります。どの決定点でも、可能な選択肢は1つだけです。これらの文法は、予測型パーサーと呼ばれます。これらは、上で示したトップダウン定義を用いた文法の手作業による生成に特に適しており、ACIS に推奨される種類の文法です。
contents.html: In general, then the production selection process may involve trial and error. If a production is selected which does not allow the successful definition of a parse tree, it is necessary to backtrack and select an alternate production until either a parse tree has been built or all possibilities have been exhausted. There is a special class of grammars, however, in which backtracking is not required. These grammars have the characteristic that they do not allow ambiguities to exist with respect to the choice of production to choose when constructing a parse tree. At any given decision point, only one possible choice exists. These grammars are called predictive parsers. They are especially suited to the hand generation of grammars using the top-down definition illustrated above and is the kind of grammar recommended for ACIS.

SDNS uses the layering principles of OSI to implement secure data transfers between computer nodes of local area and wide area networks. The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture and a set of associated specifications were developed through a multi-organizational project sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA) They are presented here as a basis for standardization of

security services in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to encourage widespread adoption of the resulting standards and the implementation of these security services into a wide spectrum of vendor products.

NIST is publishing the specifications that resulted from Phase I of the SDNS project for review and comment from potential government and commercial users of security products. The specifications are not complete or totally consistent, either internally or with a number of other security projects in the National and International Standards arena. Readers of these documents should recognize that these specifications are subject to modification for various reasons as they progress through the standards process. The sponsor and participants in the SDNS project are acknowledged for the work accomplished and their support in developing and releasing these specifications.

The SDNS project was initiated by NSA to investigate methods of implementing security in a distributed computer network. The results of this project include a set of specifications that include security services, protocols and mechanisms for protecting user data in networks that are based on the OSI computer network model. Productive security services that protect user data are specified and supportive security services, such as key management and access control, are also provided. No cryptographic algorithms are included in these specifications.

NIST is working with NSA and industry to identify and develop a framework of base standards for network security. In 1989, NIST established the OSI Security Laboratory where interested researchers from government and industry develop and demonstrate new ideas in network security. The major goals of NIST's network security activities are to:
Identify and develop security standards for open systems
Specify a key management system that supports these security standards
Encourage the development of interoperable equipment

NISTIR 90-4259 consists of three documents developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project. The Access Control Concept Document, SDN. 801, describes the principles and functions underlying the SDNS access control and authentication security services. It is a goal that the access control and authentication mechanisms designed by SDNS be adaptable to support a wide range of anticipated customer security policies.

The purpose of SDN. 802, the Access Control Specification, is to provide a common basis from which devices implementing the access control service will be able to achieve interoperability. The document also identifies points of reference for users implementing the SDNS Security Protocols for Network, Transport, or Messaging. SDN. 802 gives a functional description of the SDNS access control system and establishes a point of reference from which security protocols can make use of the access control service.
The SDN. 802 specification also provides an overview of the Access Control Information Specification (ACIS) ACIS provides a uniform
method for encoding access control information which is independent of any particular security policy. It also provides a standard algorithm for interpreting and comparing access control attributes.

The third document in this set, SDN. 802/1, ACIS Addendum 1, is an extension of the ACIS discussion provided in section 5 of SDN. 802. It furnishes a detailed explanation of the capabilities, limitations, and implementation requirements for ACIS.
The access control documents of NISTIR 90-4259 support the security protocols addressed in NISTIR 90-4250 and the key management services covered in NISTIR 90-4262.
Comments and feedback are solicited by NIST.

This paper addresses SDNS access control and, as such, represents the consensus of the Access Control Working Group (ACWG). Other SDNS working groups, such as Protocol and Systems Management have addressed the other major components of the SDNS. All of these have had a direct influence on the preliminary SDNS access control concepts that are presented in this paper

The four-tiered model for access control, described in detail in the SDNS Access Control Concept Document (SDN. 801), serves as a vehicle for defining the types of information necessary for making an
access control decision. At a high level the four-tiered model consists of:
Partition Tier - An SDNS access control division, at the highest level, of the population into
Partition Rule Based Access Control (PRBAC) Tier - Expression of the SDNS access control
information which represents a policy common to all entities in the same partition.
Local Rule Based Access Control (LRBAC) Tier - Expression of the SDNS access control
information which represents locally applicable policies or rules which govern the access to
resources owned or administered by specific organizations.
Identity Based Access Control (IBAC) Tier - Expression of the identity of the peer and
additional information about the kinds of associations that are allowed with that peer.
Primary certificates are interpretable by all SDNS components sharing a common universal. Primary
certificates are anticipated to carry access control information related to the Partition Tier, to the PRBAC tier, and to the IBAC tier. Primary certificate formats are defined uniformly.

AVs have local significance within the set of SDNS components under the jurisdiction of a common local domain authority, and are used to reflect attributes of the communicating accountable entities with which the AVs are associated. It is anticipated that auxiliary vectors will be used to carry access control information related to the LRBAC and IBAC tiers. LRBAC and IBAC information carried in AVs has the property that its syntactic and semantic significance is determined by the local domain
In this subsection, we examine the relationship between the tiers of the four-tiered model and the points where information relevant to the decisions made in each of the model's tiers is represented.
The next subsection will consider the detailed representation of the data relevant to access control as it
occurs in primary certificates, in auxiliary vectors, and in PDFs. It should be recognized that each of
these constructs also contains additional data (e g KMS-specific information and certain labeling , information interpreted only by end systems) which is not within the scope of SDNS access control.

Information relevant to the Partition tier is represented in the primary certificate. The test for common partition membership between peers attempting communication is performed wholly by PAA based on comparison between certificate contents; no PDU fields are relevant to this tier.

Primary certificate space considerations may make it necessary to carry a proper subset of PRBAC information in AVs, but this course of action would limit interoperability across jurisdiction boundaries.

3.2 Access Control Portions of the Primary Certificate
This subsection examines the portions of the primary certificate which contain information that can be

used in making an access control decision. These fields are to be contained within the primary certificate, being supplied by a central authority. Additional access control information may be placed within the locally generated AV, if it cannot be placed within the primary certificate and local doctrine
allows this. Information is placed in the primary certificate to support two of the access control system's primary axioms: the first axiom states that a maximum amount of access control information
must be contained within the primary certificate, this maximizes interoperability between different
communities within a partition; the second axiom states that sufficient access control information
must be contained within the primary certificate to allow for a meaningful access control decision to be
made, this allows communication between communities having different local authorities or those
communities which do not support the use of AVs.
The access control portions of the primary certificate must accurately and completely convey the attributes of the accountable entity which is being represented. At a minimum, the access control
portions of the primary certificate must contain enough information to support the accountable
The purpose of the AV is to supplement the access control system information contained in the primary certificate. The AV presents a mechanism to locally define, format, and process access control
data which is (a) highly volatile, (b) of use, interest, or constrained only to a small community, or (c)
extensible beyond the available field lengths in the primary certificate.
The contents of the AV are variable, depending upon local network security requirements and policies for access control. The projected contents will include information binding the AV to the SDNS
component's primary certificate, information which describes the identity, access permissions, and/or
governing local policies assigned to that entity, and data integrity check fields which will ensure any
attempt at data manipulation is detectable.
As the AV carries access control information which is presumptively more detailed (a finer level of

granularity) than that which is contained in the primary certificate. The level of system integrity provided the AV must meet the minimum level required by local network security policy for access control. The information contained in the AV must be protected in accordance with whatever policy
governs the control of that information.

The Auxiliary Vector, as stated in paragraph 3.3.1, provides supplementary information to complete a highly granular PAA process. The Primary Certificate contains information used for access control decisions at the Tier 1 (Partition) and Tier 2 (PRBAC) PAA decision levels. The AV may contain some PRBAC Data (e.g.;, if this information is needed to accurately represent the tier 3 data which is an extension of the tier 2 data). Tier 3 (LRBAC) and Tier 4 (IBAC) level data. During PAA, the primary-certificate is passed as part of the initial KMP exchange. After a TrafTic Encryption Key is formed, and if the PAA partial results are positive, KMP will exchange the AV. Local policy will determine these requirements. Once the AV data has been fully passed, PAA will complete. If positive (PAA is passed), the formed EV will be applied during PAE If PAA fails, the association is dropped.

This section describes the access control functions, sub-functions, requirements, and interfaces, for the application of SDNS access control to both the direct real-time and staged delivery communications services. The processes of Peer Access Approval (PAA) and Peer Access Enforcement (PAE) are examined in detail. The relationships between PAA, PAE, KMP, and the SPs are explained. Only brief, functional descriptions of the SPs and KMP are given here, the reader is directed to reference the
particular protocol specification desired for further details. Several figures are used to aid in

representing these relationships, and along with the accompanying functional descriptions give a good layout for how access control fits into the overall SDNS. The modular allocation of functions described
in this section is for expository purposes only and is not meant to imply any restrictions on the
The PAA process is the process which evaluates the peer security attribute information of the two
communicating peer endpoints in an attempt to determine a commonly held set of security attributes

This commonly held set of security attribute information can be further pared down through the application of local configuration information to yield an Enforcement Vector (EV). It is this EV which the PAE process will use later to screen against PDUs.

The PAA process is called from the Key Management Protocol’s (KMP) Key Management Application Process (KMAPKthe KMAP is defined in detail in the KMP documentation: SDN.902 and SDN. 903) to perform its functionality, an exception to this is the Message Security Protocol (MSP) (explained in section 4.3). Two specific services of the KMAP make use of the PAA process; Exchange Credentials
and Attribute Negotiations. Figure 4.1 shows this relationship.
The Exchange Credentials service will call PAA to evaluate both peers’ primary certificate

information. All of the access control relevant primary certificate information will be evaluated at this time. If no further access control information is to be exchanged, the PAA process will yield a result (PAA Result) which will be returned to the KMAP. If additional access control information is to be exchanged the Attribute Negotiations service will call PAA to evaluate both peers’ additional access control information (in the form of an AV). Upon the completion of PAA a result will be returned to the KMAP (PAA Result). It is this result which will determine the remainder of the processing which the KMAP must perform. When any of the PAA checks fail, PAA Result = Fail and any audit messages required by local policy will be generated as control is returned to the KMAP. The following
sections describe the details of the PAA process, figure 4.2 illustrates the functions which are

The Enter PAA function is the point at which the KMAP will transfer control over to the PAA process so that a comparison between peer security attributes can be made in an attempt to determine an

allowable set of these attributes, which will be bound to the association being formed between accountable peer entities. The allowable intersecting set of security attributes will be represented in an EV, which will be used later in the PAE process. The Enter PAA function will call the Check
Universal function to perform its processing.
The Check Universal process ensures that the universal being used in both the local and remote primary certificates is identical. If the universals are identical then Univ Check = Pass and the

Decrypt Certificate function is called to perform its processing If the universals are not identical then Univ Check = Fail. When Univ Check = Fail an audit message may be generated and the control of the processing will be returned to the KMAP.

The Peer Access Enforcement (PAE) process provides for the continuous enforcement of the access control decision made in the PAA process. PAE determines if the security sensitivity of a data packet, represented in a PDU’s attributes, falls within an allowable set of security attributes determined during PAA. The enforcement mechanism becomes involved when peer Security Protocols (SP) attempt to transfer data. The full suite of PAE processing is only required when the label contained on a specific piece of data (either imported or exported) is an explicit label. When implicit labeling is being used, only a limited subset of PAE is used, the PAA process provides sufficient access control

The PAE process is called from the SP to perform its functionality The SP acts as a gate keeper for all data packets, both incoming and outgoing. When the SP receives a packet for processing it checks to

At the appropriate time in the SP processing the PAE process will be called to perform its processing. Figure 4.3 illustrates the functions which the PAE process will perform. The requirement for the Access Control Information Specification has been established as a result of the Access Control Working Group's (ACWG) investigation of various Partitions. This tool may be
applied to all Partitions, but as yet a detailed investigation of the Security Attribute structures of all
Investigations have shown that the Security Attributes of many environments are both hierarchical

and non-hierarchical in nature and can be represented as a tree structure. This organizational scheme posed some problems when trying to represent this data in a Primary Certificate or in an Auxiliary Vector. If the data is broken down into tiers and an entire tier is represented contiguously before moving to the next tier, ambiguities may arise when trying to associate lower tier attributes with the current tier being examined. On the other hand representing each branch of the tree completely and independently requires too much space. More importantly, it has been found that without some uniform method for encoding and comparing access control data many SDNS implementations would
require software specific to their local security policy. With this set of issues to be resolved, the
set out to develop the Access Control Information Specification (ACIS).
ACIS is a tool to be supported by vendors who develop SDNS components supporting access control and to be used by SDNS customers. ACIS provides several useful functions;
(a) It provides an approach to enforcing access control which is independent of any particular
security policy, leading to a savings in development costs for an implementation;
(b) It provides a uniform method for representing access control information through the use of its
(c) It provides a standard algorithm for interpreting and comparing access control attributes.
ACIS is based upon the theory of predictive parsing The grammar is a form of an LL(1) grammar. A more detailed description on ACIS can be found in the SDNS Access Control Specification, Addendum

ACIS is designed to handle problems that arise when the Security Attributes of a particular system have certain characteristics. The most important of these characteristics is that the system Security Attributes can be expressed in a tree structure, implying hierarchy and interdependence. A second
characteristic of the system is that its access control must be able to be performed as an intersection
process of the attributes of the two entities that wish to communicate.
